paragraphs.text: English fork of dsh-forget-session — a two-step Forget session action for DeepSeek Harness
# dsh-forget-session-en
**English fork of dsh-forget-session by 2026heshao.** This fork translates the UI text, code comment
s, documentation, and error messages to English, and uses its own package, plugin-row, service, and
slot IDs so it can be installed alongside the original instead of colliding with it. The behavior is
otherwise identical to upstream v2.2.1.
See docs/verification-checklist.md for the verification and troubleshooting checklist.
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that adds a **"Forget session"** item to the session row's "…" menu
and removes that session completely from the sidebar and from disk. Data accumulated by the Lingxu m
emory plugin is not affected. It works on both the desktop and web builds (the plugin UI runs in the
same browser rendering layer in both, so behavior is identical).
> **Compatibility**: fully tested on DeepSeek Harness 44.7.0 (host bundles `@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-
protocol@0.2.1-rc.2` / cordis 4.0.5); the declared peer range `>=0.1.5-rc.1` still covers it, and th
is version needs no code changes.
## Features
Adds exactly one item, in the **session row "…" menu**:
- **"Forget session"** (order 500, placed after the official "Pin / Rename / Branch / Archive" items

)
- **Two-step confirmation** after clicking: the row becomes "Click again to confirm", and only the

next click executes
(everything happens inside the menu, with no dialog; failures are shown directl

y on this row, never silently)
- On success the row disappears and a top Toast reports the deletion
summary (how many artifacts were deleted, how many warnings)
| Deleted object | Method |

| Running work | Official `workspace/session-stop` waterfall (stopActivity archive path) |
| **Live
session (inside the Session store)** | Official `entry.detach()` internal channel: `store.delete` +

`attachments.delete` + `emitDisposed` (new in v2.2; see root cause 3 below) |
| Workspace accounting

(`sessionIds` in workspace.json) | Official `detachSession` channel (domain write chain) |
| Archiv

e set / pinned set | Official `unarchiveSession` / `unpinSession` |
| Session log directory `~/.dsh/
sessions/<project key>/<id>` | Whole-directory delete (including `_no-cwd`, legacy unprefixed layout

s, and in-use retries) |
| Projection cache shard `~/.dsh/storages/session_projcache/sessions/<id>.j

son` | Delete |
| Table entry in the projection cache `~/.dsh/storages/session_projcache.json` | Rea

d-modify-write; everything else is preserved as-is |
| Resurrected files (leftover handles / recreat
ed by late writes) | The Host "resurrection guard" deletes them again automatically within a ~2-minu

te window |
| Sidebar session row (client session list) | Official `sessions.handleSessionRemoved(id
)` + `sessions.refresh()` |
**Data left untouched**: Lingxu memory (`~/.dsh/.dsh-memory`), attachments, and any other session.
## What was fixed (why deleted sessions returned to "Ungrouped")

"Ungrouped" = ids in the client session list − the union of all `workspace.sessionIds`.
After gather
ing evidence package by package from the official source, three resurrection paths were confirmed:
| Root cause | Mechanism | Countermeasure |
| **Windows live-deletion race** | Once a session has been opened there is a write handle / cross-pr
ocess lease: `rm` on the directory reports EBUSY/EPERM, v1 failed silently → files remained → the re
gistry re-adopted them after a restart; and a late append from the live teardown after deletion coul
d **recreate the deleted directory** | **Verification re-check** after deletion, with backoff retrie
s for in-use errors; set up a **resurrection guard**: exponential backoff starting at 2s (capped at
32s) and periodic re-checks for a total window of ~130s, immediately deleting any recreated director

y |
| **Client list resurrection** | The Host's `session.list` still lists live sessions; any client
`refreshList` (triggered on reconnect) merges the deleted rows back | After deletion, call the offi
cial `sessions.refresh()` to reload the baseline, so the resurrected row is removed again before it

becomes visible |
| **Live entry never detached (root-fixed in v2.2)** | `SessionStore` has no publi
c remove API: once a session enters the store, `session.list` (which merges live + persisted session
s) always lists it — after deletion it **immediately** returns to "Ungrouped"; and the persistence w
riter holds a write handle that keeps the disk busy, so `rm` gets EBUSY and even the resurrection gu
ard deleting for ~130s is wasted | Use the official `entry.detach()` carried by every store entry (=
`store.delete` + `attachments.delete` + `emitDisposed`): this both removes the row from `session.li
st` (official `api-session/removed` frame) and releases the persistence write handle — only then doe
s the disk deletion actually work |
[该节后续省略]
## How it works (for maintainers)

- **Host half** (`lib/index.js`): a `TypertRemoteService` named `forgetSessionEn` with
`inject: ["wo

rkspaceRegistry"]`. `delete()` goes through the official state channels
(stop / unarchive / unpin /

**live detach** / detach), then deletes disk artifacts
using the same path algorithm as `session-per

sistence-jsonl` (`projectKey` +
`encodeSegment`) (retrying in-use errors with backoff + verification

re-check),
cleans the projection cache, and finally sets up the resurrection guard. It never
edits

`workspace.json` by hand — accounting is done through the registry's official
mutate write chain. Li

ve removal obtains the entry via
`ctx.get("sessions").store` (a public class field Map) and calls `e

ntry.detach()`,
which is equivalent to the official `SessionStore.detachEntered`.
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations

- The official DSH design is "archive sessions, never delete them" (see the
dsh-client-ui-workspace

README); this plugin is a user-level addition beyond the
official channels.
- If the deleted session

is live in this process: buffered events are first
`flush`ed to disk, then the session is detached

from the store via
`entry.detach()` (the official dispose channel closes the persistence write
handl

e). Late writes from the teardown within the guard window (~130s) are
deleted afterwards. Deleting i

dle sessions is recommended.
- For the session search index (`session-query-sqlite`), when `openAt`

is not
`never`, deleted session rows converge automatically on the next `_reconcile`
(any search) —

the persisted list no longer contains the id, and the index clears
it through `persistentDeletes`; `

openAt: never` (the default) is in-memory and
self-heals.
